title: Time, Speed and Distance
tagline: Year 2 — Speed = distance ÷ time, unit conversion, average speed and late/early arrivals

introduction.overview: Speed is how much distance is covered in a unit of time: speed = distance ÷ time. From this single relation come distance = speed × time and time = distance ÷ speed. The skill lies in handling units (km/h and m/s), average speed over unequal parts, and problems where a change in speed changes the time taken by a given amount.
introduction.placementRelevance: Time, speed and distance questions are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds. They are the base for relative speed, trains and boats and streams.
introduction.realWorldContext: Planning a journey, estimating arrival times and comparing the speeds of different vehicles use the same formula.

learningObjectives: Use S = D/T in all three forms
Compute average speed for equal distances, equal times and unequal parts
Solve problems with a change in speed and a change in time
Use the inverse proportion of speed and time for a fixed distance

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: For a fixed distance, speed and time are inversely proportional. Time in minutes ÷ 60 gives hours.

coreDefinitions: Speed = Distance ÷ Time. Units: km/h, m/s.
Conversion: 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and 1 m/s = 18/5 km/h.
Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time.
For equal distances at speeds x and y: average = 2xy/(x + y). For equal times: (x + y)/2.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Speed tells you how many kilometres you get per hour. If you drive faster you take less time for the same distance. For a fixed distance, speed × time is constant, so doubling the speed halves the time.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: For a late/early problem, write two equations: distance ÷ speed₁ and distance ÷ speed₂ differ by the total time difference. Solve for distance.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Basic relations
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: D = S × T;  S = D/T;  T = D/S

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Average speed (equal distances)
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Half the distance at each speed.

mainNarrative: Always keep units consistent. If speed is in km/h, distance must be in km and time in hours. To change km/h to m/s multiply by 5/18; for the reverse multiply by 18/5. So 72 km/h = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s.
Average speed is total distance over total time, never the simple average of the speeds unless the times are equal. For equal distances, use 2xy/(x + y): 30 km/h and 20 km/h give 24 km/h.

For unequal parts, compute the time of each part. If 1/3 of the journey is at 20 km/h, 1/3 at 30 km/h and 1/3 at 60 km/h, the time per unit distance is (1/3)(1/20 + 1/30 + 1/60) = 1/30, so the average speed is 30 km/h.
In late/early problems, write D/S₁ − D/S₂ equal to the total time difference. A train 15 minutes late at 40 km/h and 15 minutes early at 60 km/h: D/40 − D/60 = 30/60 gives D = 60 km.

If a speed change gives a time change, use the ratio method. Increasing speed by 20% makes the time 1/1.2 of before, so the saved time is 1/6 of the original; if that is 20 minutes, the usual time is 120 minutes.

deepDiveAspects.title: Why the average is harmonic
deepDiveAspects.content: Equal distances at two speeds take different times. The slower speed is used longer, so it weighs more, and the average is less than the simple mean.

deepDiveAspects.title: Speed ratio and time ratio
deepDiveAspects.content: If speeds are in the ratio a : b, the times for the same distance are in the ratio b : a. A 3 : 4 speed ratio gives a 4 : 3 time ratio.

solvedExamples.title: Average speed
solvedExamples.question: A man travels half the distance of a 120 km journey at 30 km/h and the other half at 20 km/h. Find his average speed.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: More time is spent at the slower speed.

solvedExamples.title: Late and early
solvedExamples.question: A train would reach 15 minutes late at 40 km/h and 15 minutes early at 60 km/h. Find the distance.
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: D/S₁ − D/S₂ = difference of arrival times.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The two arrival times are 30 minutes apart.

solvedExamples.title: Speed change
solvedExamples.question: If a man increases his speed by 20%, he saves 20 minutes on a journey. Find the usual time.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: A 20% faster speed saves 1/6 of the time.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Saying 20 minutes saved is 20% of the time.

shortcutMethods.title: Inverse proportion shortcut

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Set up equations for every problem.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: For a fixed distance, speed ratio a : b means time ratio b : a. Speed rises by p/q makes time fall by p/(p + q) of the old time.

rulesForApplication: Average speed = total D ÷ total T.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Subtracting arrival times in the wrong order.
commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Total difference is the sum of late and early.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Taking the percent change of time equal to speed.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Average speed for equal distances must lie between the two speeds, closer to the smaller one.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: This is the foundation for trains and boats.

intermediate.question: A man travels the first half of a 120 km journey at 30 km/h and the second half at 20 km/h. His average speed is
intermediate.explanation: Times: 60/30 = 2 h and 60/20 = 3 h. Total 5 h. Speed = 120 ÷ 5 = 24 km/h.

intermediate.question: Walking at 5/6 of his usual speed, a man takes 12 minutes more. His usual time is
intermediate.explanation: T × 6/5 = T + 12 gives T/5 = 12, so T = 60 minutes.

advanced.explanation: New time = T/1.2. T − T/1.2 = T/6 = 20, so T = 120 minutes.

placementStyle.question: A boy reaches school 10 minutes late at 4 km/h and 10 minutes early at 6 km/h. The distance to school is
A car runs at 60 km/h without stoppages and 50 km/h including stoppages. The stoppage per hour is
placementStyle.explanation: In 1 hour including stops it covers 50 km, which takes 50/60 h of running. Stoppage = 1 − 5/6 = 1/6 h = 10 minutes.

placementStyle.question: A man travels 300 km by train at 60 km/h and 200 km by bus at 40 km/h. His average speed is
placementStyle.explanation: Times: 5 h and 5 h. Total 10 h for 500 km. Average = 50 km/h.
